---
title: "Entry point"
subtitle: "The one function a document calls, and the three selectors every directive takes."
description: "display-table, the shape of the data it accepts, the order directives apply in, and the column, row, and group selectors."
---

## Entry point

```typst
display-table(
  data,                    // first positional: rows or columns
  ..directives,            // any number of directives, applied in order
  theme: theme-default(),  // option dictionary
  spec: none,              // a built specification, rendered instead
)
```

`data` is either an array of dictionaries, one per row, or a dictionary of equal-length arrays, one per column.
Every row gains a reserved `_index` key holding its position in the input, which is what row predicates read.

Directives are plain dictionaries applied in the order written.
For a given cell and property the last matching directive wins, so "format the column, then override a few rows" reads the way it is written.

## Selectors

Three arguments recur throughout, and all three accept the same shapes.

| Argument | Accepts |
| --- | --- |
| `columns` | `auto`, a name, an array of names, or a predicate `name => bool`. |
| `rows` | `auto`, an index, an array of indices, or a predicate `row => bool`. |
| `groups` | `auto`, a label, an array of labels, or a predicate `label => bool`. |

: Selector shapes {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[20,80]"}

Every predicate takes exactly one argument.
Typst closures fail on arity mismatch, and `row => row.margin < 0.05` is what people write, so row position travels on `row._index` rather than as a second parameter.
